nodes.assess: The fence around a triangular pen is 40 feet long. Two sides of the pen are 12 feet and 15 feet. How long is the third side?

proposed_edges.rationale: The test problem adds the known sides 12 and 15.
The learner subtracts the known sides from the total length around to get the missing side.
The test problem subtracts the known sides total 27 from the perimeter 40.

nodes.name: Tell perimeter from area
nodes.statement: Perimeter measures the length of a figure's boundary in length units; area measures how many unit squares cover it, in square units. They are different measures of the same figure.
nodes.assess: A rectangle drawn on a grid is 5 units long and 3 units wide. One of the numbers 15 and 16 is its area and the other is its perimeter. Which is which, and what is the unit of each?

proposed_edges.rationale: The other measure is the number of unit squares that cover the figure.
The test problem needs the area of a 5 by 3 rectangle, found as 5 times 3.
The units differ because area is counted in square units while perimeter is counted in length units.
The test problem has a rectangle on a grid whose area is found by counting squares.
One of the two measures is the length of the boundary, measured in length units.
The test problem finds the perimeter of the 5 by 3 rectangle by adding its sides.
The test problem needs the perimeter of a 5 by 3 rectangle, found from its length and width.

nodes.name: Exhibit rectangles with the same area and different perimeters
nodes.statement: Rectangles with the same area can have different perimeters; produce such rectangles by choosing different whole-number side-length pairs with the same product.
nodes.assess: Draw two rectangles on grid paper that each have an area of 12 square units but have different perimeters. Give each perimeter.

proposed_edges.rationale: Each rectangle's area is its length times its width, which must equal the chosen product.
The learner draws rectangles on grid paper whose area is a given product.
Side-length pairs with the same product are chosen by recalling products, such as 3 x 4 and 2 x 6 for 12.
The learner gives each rectangle's perimeter from its length and width.
The statement contrasts the two measures, holding area fixed while the perimeter changes.

nodes.name: Exhibit rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas
nodes.statement: Rectangles with the same perimeter can have different areas; produce such rectangles by choosing different whole-number side-length pairs with the same sum.
nodes.assess: Draw two rectangles on grid paper that each have a perimeter of 16 units but have different areas. Give each area.

proposed_edges.rationale: Side-length pairs with the same sum are chosen by adding trial lengths and widths.
Choosing whole-number pairs with the same sum, such as 8, uses recalled sums.
The learner gives each rectangle's area as its length times its width.
The test problem halves the perimeter 16 to get the sum 8 of length and width.
Each rectangle's perimeter is two lengths plus two widths, which must equal the chosen perimeter.
The statement contrasts the two measures, holding perimeter fixed while the area changes.
